# GROUNDED EVIDENCE BRIEF (write ONLY from this; cite [PMID: n] from included studies)

- Included studies: 4 (CAR-T 3, BsAb 1); 4 uncertain pending full text.
- Screened 50 verified records of 50 identified.
- Risk of bias (overall): {'Serious': 2, 'Some concerns': 1, 'No information': 1}.
- No head-to-head RCT between CAR-T vs BsAb exists (indirect comparison).

## Pooled estimates (random-effects)
- >=Complete response [ALL]: 64.5% (95% CI 61.6–67.3; I²=9%; k=2)

## GRADE certainty (per outcome)
- Overall response rate (ORR): Very Low (start Low; 3 downgrade(s); n=1)
- >=Complete response (>=CR): Low (start High; 2 downgrade(s); n=2)
- MRD negativity: No data (start —; 0 downgrade(s); n=0)
- Progression-free survival (median): No data (start —; 0 downgrade(s); n=0)
- Overall survival (median): No data (start —; 0 downgrade(s); n=0)
- CRS (any grade): Low (start High; 2 downgrade(s); n=1)
- CRS (grade >=3): No data (start —; 0 downgrade(s); n=0)
- ICANS / neurotoxicity: Low (start High; 2 downgrade(s); n=1)
- Infections (grade >=3): Low (start High; 2 downgrade(s); n=1)
- Neutropenia (grade >=3): No data (start —; 0 downgrade(s); n=0)
- Treatment-related mortality: No data (start —; 0 downgrade(s); n=0)

## Named pivotal trials captured
- CARTITUDE-4, MajesTEC-9, MagnetisMM

## Included studies (citable PMIDs — cite as [PMID: n])
- [PMID: 42227005] (?) Real-World Incidence and Management of Non-Immune Effector Cell-Associated Neurotoxicity S
- [PMID: 42212933] (?) Teclistamab in Multiple Myeloma with One to Three Previous Lines of Therapy.
- [PMID: 42169674] (?) Real-world outcomes of cilta-cel versus BCMA-targeting bispecific antibodies in relapsed/r
- [PMID: 42163304] (?) Standard-of-care ciltacabtagene autoleucel in earlier versus later lines of therapy for re

draft.abstract_background: BCMA-directed immunotherapies, including chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy and bispecific antibodies (BsAb), have expanded the treatment landscape for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma. However, the comparative effectiveness and safety of these modalities remain uncertain, and no head-to-head randomized controlled trial between CAR-T and BsAb exists.
draft.abstract_results: From 50 verified records identified and screened, 4 studies were included (3 CAR-T, 1 BsAb), with an additional 4 records uncertain pending full-text review. Among the included reports were the pivotal trials/programs CARTITUDE-4, MajesTEC-9, and MagnetisMM, alongside real-world analyses [PMID: 42169674; PMID: 42163304; PMID: 42212933; PMID: 42227005]. Pooled across 2 studies, the rate of at least complete response (>=CR) was 64.5% (95% CI 61.6–67.3; I²=9%). Overall risk of bias across included studies was rated as serious in 2 studies, some concerns in 1, and no information in 1. No data were available for MRD negativity, progression-free survival, overall survival, grade >=3 CRS, grade >=3 neutropenia, or treatment-related mortality.
draft.abstract_conclusions: Available evidence suggests a pooled >=CR rate of approximately 64.5% with BCMA-directed immunotherapy in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma, but certainty is limited and direct comparison between CAR-T and BsAb relies on indirect evidence. Several key efficacy and safety outcomes were not reported in the included studies.
draft.introduction: Relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma remains a therapeutic challenge, and BCMA-directed immunotherapies—including CAR-T therapy and bispecific antibodies (BsAb)—have emerged as treatment options. Pivotal trials and programs such as CARTITUDE-4, MajesTEC-9, and MagnetisMM have evaluated these approaches. To date, no head-to-head randomized controlled trial directly comparing CAR-T with BsAb has been conducted, so any comparison between the two modalities rests on indirect evidence. This systematic review synthesizes the available evidence on the efficacy and safety of these therapies. We identified 50 records, all of which were verified and screened, yielding 4 included studies (3 CAR-T and 1 BsAb), with 4 additional records remaining uncertain pending full-text assessment [PMID: 42227005; PMID: 42212933; PMID: 42169674; PMID: 42163304].
draft.discussion: In this synthesis of 4 included studies, the pooled rate of at least complete response (>=CR) was 64.5% (95% CI 61.6–67.3) across 2 studies, with low statistical heterogeneity (I²=9%). The included evidence encompassed real-world and trial-based reports, including teclistamab in patients with one to three prior lines of therapy [PMID: 42212933] and real-world outcomes of cilta-cel versus BCMA-targeting bispecific antibodies [PMID: 42169674], as well as analyses of standard-of-care ciltacabtagene autoleucel across lines of therapy [PMID: 42163304] and neurotoxicity management [PMID: 42227005]. Importantly, no head-to-head randomized comparison between CAR-T and BsAb was available, meaning that comparisons between these modalities are indirect. Several outcomes of clinical importance—including MRD negativity, progression-free survival, overall survival, grade >=3 CRS, grade >=3 neutropenia, and treatment-related mortality—were not reported by the included studies, limiting the scope of conclusions. The overall risk of bias was serious in 2 studies, of some concern in 1, and unclear in 1. These limitations, together with the small number of included studies, should be considered when interpreting the pooled estimates.
